title: Native-first personal access: integration scope and candidate acceptance
body:
## Problem / outcome

Deliver personal subscription-backed access with LiteLLM → CLIProxyAPI, native
personal Usage and native Langfuse. Reuse upstream accounts, keys, limits and
reporting; organize ProxyLens work around configuration and integration gaps.

## Revision and current state

Revised in place on October 29, 2026 with owner approval. Original issue bodies are archived in
`docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`. Existing code implements
Keycloak/group/custom-gateway contracts; its evidence is preserved, not relabeled.
ADR 0002 remains proposed until the candidate is accepted.

## Scope

- Own the shared scope in `docs/specs/litellm-poc.md` and record choices needed by
  setup: actual client/model, native edition, ordinary role and enabled policies.
- Coordinate #2 configuration, #8 Langfuse, #7 one integration acceptance pass,
  and #6 production readiness/cutover. #5/#9 consolidate into #2; #4 into #7.
- Keep #3 optional diagnostics and #10 deferred reporting-gap work.
- Review native behavior and concrete gaps before accepting the candidate. Native
  features require no custom implementation or repeated upstream test suite.

## Dependencies

#2/#8 configure the candidate, #7 supplies A1–A6 evidence, #6 prepares production
readiness. Scope decisions happen first; candidate acceptance precedes separately
approved cutover. No dependency on closing optional/deferred tickets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Required client/model, native feature scope and configuration choices are
  recorded. Additional requirements are explicit, not inferred from old contracts.
- [ ] #2/#8 deliver the configured candidate and #7 completes the shared A1–A6
  checks: native access, client protocol, ownership/usage, controls, telemetry and
  CPAMP-independent native Usage.
- [ ] Native UI gaps and observed limitations are reviewed. Wrong ownership,
  privacy leakage or broken required client behavior blocks acceptance; custom
  work is scoped only for an agreed gap.
- [ ] Deferred handoff P1–P13 scenarios are recorded as deferred/conditional, not
  passed. No strict-budget, lossless-accounting or exactly-once-delivery claim is
  made from a smoke check.
- [ ] Owner accepts or rejects the candidate with evidence. On acceptance, update
  ADR statuses, glossary and guidance together; authorize cutover separately in #6.

## Non-goals

Reimplementing native LiteLLM features; certifying all upstream internals; advanced
statistics, custom accounting store/exporter, mandatory CPAMP or immediate cutover.

## Operational notes

Preserve historical group ownership and old proof limitations. CPA remains the
provider/OAuth boundary; CPAMP is the only queue consumer when enabled. Langfuse
is observability, not authorization/accounting. Follow-up guarantees require their
own scoped evidence. Update `DEVELOPMENT.md` with decisions and actual results.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md`; `docs/planning/architecture-rebaseline-2026-10-29.md`;
`docs/adr/0002-litellm-personal-usage.md`; `docs/live-acceptance.md`.

title: Configure LiteLLM → CPA: deployment, native accounts, keys, limits, and Usage
body:
## Problem / outcome

Configure a reproducible LiteLLM → CPA deployment with native accounts, personal
keys, limits, persistent spend/history and native Usage. These are upstream
features to configure, not new ProxyLens services to implement.

## Revision and current state

Approved October 29, 2026 revision of the Compose foundation; absorbs native
account/key configuration from #5/#9. Original contracts are archived in
`docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`. Current `compose.yaml`
deploys Keycloak/custom services/CPA/CPAMP, not LiteLLM; preserve its runtime state.

## Scope

- Isolated candidate Compose/config, LiteLLM database, CPA inference route,
  necessary coordination dependencies, secrets and native UI ingress.
- Pin the actual image/digest, schema and configuration; record the chosen
  edition. The research snapshot is not an installed-image guarantee.
- Configure native onboarding and ordinary-user role, users A/B, personal keys
  (including a second key for A), allowed models and selected native limits.
- Enable native persisted usage/Usage UI; set explicit CPA alias pricing where
  needed. Keep content capture disabled; no new ledger or dashboard backend.
- Supply native secret/callback configuration seams for #8 and fixture for #7.

## Dependencies

#1 actual client/model, deployment endpoints, selected policies and CPA sharing
decision. #8 owns Langfuse integration settings; #7 owns the shared behavioral
checks. #6 owns production backup/restore and cutover. No mandatory CPAMP profile.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Documented commands start the pinned candidate with persistent state,
  healthchecks and private data/management services; existing state is isolated.
- [ ] Native ordinary-user login, user-owned keys, selected model/limit policies
  and native Usage are configured in the chosen edition. Record documented native
  defaults/semantics; any paid dependency needs a visible product decision.
- [ ] Admin-created personal keys explicitly identify their intended owner; avoid
  admin-viewer roles for personal access. CPA service/admin and personal keys are
  distinct, server-side secrets are not committed or exposed to browsers.
- [ ] CPA alias prices, native logging/privacy options and storage ownership are
  recorded. Optional coordination services are included only when required.
- [ ] A startup/native-login smoke check succeeds; provide the reproducible A/B
  fixture to #7. Do not duplicate its full integration acceptance here.
- [ ] CPAMP is optional, with no second consumer of an existing CPA queue.
  Candidate setup/teardown and state-preserving rollback are documented.

## Non-goals

Custom user/key/policy services, custom reporting database or UI, native-feature
unit suites, provider OAuth replacement, HA or production cutover.

## Operational notes

Reuse CPA deployment/secrets patterns. Record exact versions/configuration and
dependency ownership in candidate deployment docs and `DEVELOPMENT.md`. Preserve
the current deployment until #6's approved cutover.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md`; `compose.yaml`; `deploy/cliproxyapi/`;
`docs/deployment.md`; `docs/dependency-pins.md`.

title: Optional CPA/CPAMP diagnostics: correlation and operator history
body:
## Problem / outcome

Optionally retain CPA-side history/account diagnostics when operators need them.
Personal keys, ownership and native Usage must work independently of CPAMP.

## Revision and current state

Approved optional disposition, October 29, 2026. The original mandatory-correlation
contract is preserved in `docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`.
`docs/correlation.md`, `docs/cpamp-contract.md` and `docs/live-acceptance.md`
retain implemented joins and unfinished proof gates; this change does not pass them.

## Scope

Activate only when #1 selects provider-account diagnostics. Reuse CPAMP and the
existing read adapter where compatible. Prove observed-ID joins only for any
diagnostic enrichment actually displayed; retain explicit missing/ambiguous joins.

## Dependencies

#2 configured candidate, #7 observed CPA identifiers. Not a prerequisite for
personal reporting, accounting or candidate acceptance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A concrete operator need is selected before implementation starts.
- [ ] The retained CPAMP version, history source and collector owner are recorded;
  CPAMP alone consumes that CPA queue.
- [ ] Displayed enriched rows use proven observed-ID joins; shared credentials,
  timestamps and models are never used to guess personal ownership.
- [ ] Diagnostic outage/gaps are visible and do not block healthy inference or
  personal Usage. Management controls and credentials stay operator-only.

## Non-goals

Mandatory CPAMP integration, a new collector, full join certification when no
enrichment is used, or adding CPA/CPAMP and LiteLLM totals as independent usage.

## Operational notes

Remain optional when unselected. Preserve existing history and one-consumer
ownership; backup/retention belongs to the selected operator deployment in #6.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md`; `docs/correlation.md`; `docs/cpamp-contract.md`.

title: Consolidated into #7: native usage integration checks
body:
## Problem / outcome

Consolidate personal usage verification into the single integration acceptance
task #7. Native LiteLLM persistence/Usage does not require a new ProxyLens
accounting adapter, canonical schema, normalization worker or replay store.

## Revision and current state

Approved consolidation into #7, October 29, 2026. Original CPAMP read/export spec and
metadata are archived in `docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`.
The implemented `src/proxylens/cpamp.py` and `docs/cpamp-contract.md` remain
available for optional #3; old evidence/limitations remain unchanged.

## Scope

Move the necessary CPA response → native retained record → personal-total sample
check into #7 A3. Future custom field capture/read/rebuild work belongs to #10
only if native reporting lacks an agreed requirement.

## Dependencies

#7 owns the sample check; #2 configures native persistence. #10 is conditional.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] #7 includes sample ownership/usage reconciliation and persisted-record restart
  evidence; no separate native accounting test suite remains in this issue.
- [ ] Original CPAMP contract and its unfinished evidence are preserved.
- Disposition: close as **not planned / consolidated into #7**, not as successful
  implementation of the old or replacement runtime acceptance criteria.

## Non-goals

New accounting infrastructure, native full replay/crash-loss certification, or
claiming a native callback guarantees retained/rebuildable data.

## Operational notes

No runtime/data deletion follows consolidation. #6 owns native database recovery;
any stronger durability guarantee must be scoped and measured separately.

title: Consolidated into #2: native account and role configuration
body:
## Problem / outcome

Use native LiteLLM accounts and ordinary-user roles. Fold their setup into #2
instead of maintaining a standalone identity implementation/test project.

## Revision and current state

Approved consolidation into #2, October 29, 2026. Original Keycloak issue #5 is archived
in `docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`. `deploy/keycloak/`,
`src/proxylens/identity.py`, `oidc.py`, `keycloak.py` and `docs/identity.md`
remain current-runtime evidence until approved cutover.

## Scope

#2 configures native onboarding/login and the selected ordinary role; #7 A1
checks the deployed login and representative own-only access. Accept native
password/account flows without rebuilding or duplicating their upstream tests.

## Dependencies

#2 setup and #7 shared integration acceptance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Native role/login setup is included in #2 and the small isolation check in #7.
- [ ] Original Keycloak contract/history is retained for current runtime maintenance.
- Disposition: close as **not planned / consolidated into #2**, not proof that
  original or replacement runtime identity criteria passed.

## Non-goals

Custom identity service, Keycloak synchronization, SSO, complete native account
recovery test matrices, or automatic retirement of existing Keycloak state.

## Operational notes

Privileged roles are not a workaround for personal access. Native setup belongs
to #2; any separate reporting session is conditional #10 work. #6 owns migration.

title: Production readiness: backup, restore, and controlled cutover
body:
## Problem / outcome

Make this deployment recoverable and perform an approved cutover after candidate
acceptance. Test our state handling and migration, not all LiteLLM internals.

## Revision and current state

Approved October 29, 2026 revision. Original operations spec is archived in
`docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`. `docs/operations.md` and
`docs/deployment.md` describe the existing custom services, not native guarantees.

## Scope

- Inventory native user/key/budget/history state, CPA OAuth/configuration and
  selected telemetry/diagnostic stores; document secret and retention ownership.
- Document and rehearse populated backup/restore and version/schema-compatible
  upgrade/rollback for the selected deployment.
- Prepare key issuance, historical-data handling, ingress switch and rollback;
  execute only after #1 candidate acceptance and separate cutover approval.
- Reuse #7 integration evidence and record native limitations. Add load benchmarks
  or accounting fault injection only for an explicit workload/guarantee.

## Dependencies

Readiness preparation begins after #2. #7/#8 supply integration/telemetry results.
#1 accepts the candidate before production cutover. #3/#10 matter only if selected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every selected state/secret has a backup and retention owner; actual retention
  values are recorded rather than inherited from old services by assumption.
- [ ] A populated restore recovers users, personal-key ownership, retained history
  and budget state; verify with a small native login/history/request check.
- [ ] Upgrade/rollback instructions identify matching binary/schema/state versions,
  incompatible migrations and how to restore the previous ingress safely.
- [ ] Health distinguishes inference, native history availability and telemetry;
  reuse #7's restart/optional-dependency checks rather than repeat a fault matrix.
- [ ] Native delivery/accounting/limit behavior and accepted limitations are
  documented. Stronger guarantees need explicit scope and supporting tests.
- [ ] Cutover plan issues replacement keys where required, preserves old group
  history or separates the accounting epoch, defines rollback triggers and keeps
  recoverable old state. Do not infer personal owners from old key creators.
- [ ] After owner approval, execute cutover and repeat the small essential client,
  login/usage and telemetry checks; retire superseded services only after success.

## Non-goals

HA, broad upstream crash-loss/overshoot certification, capacity benchmarks without
a target workload, silent state deletion, or production-request replay.

## Operational notes

The proposed 90/365/90-day retention values are starting options, not upstream
defaults. Optional CPAMP remains the sole queue consumer. Keep content capture
disabled. Update deployment docs and `DEVELOPMENT.md` with tested restore commands,
accepted limitations and cutover results.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md`; `docs/operations.md`; `docs/deployment.md`.

title: Integration acceptance: actual client, personal usage, controls, and telemetry
body:
## Problem / outcome

Verify our configured LiteLLM → CPA → native Usage/Langfuse integration with one
small end-to-end fixture. Native features are reused; this checks configuration,
provider compatibility and trusted mappings rather than retesting LiteLLM itself.

## Revision and current state

Approved October 29, 2026 revision; absorbs usage verification from #4 and shared
account/key/UI checks. Original gateway issue is archived in
`docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`. Existing gateway tests and
`scripts/live-acceptance.py` supply reusable scenarios, not candidate pass evidence.

## Scope

Run shared plan A1–A6 with users A/B, a second personal key for A, one service-owned
CPA key, actual client/version and a separate Langfuse test project. Share request
results across checks. Prefer a reproducible runbook; write regression tests for
our custom glue or a concrete defect, not native CRUD internals.

## Dependencies

#2 configured stack, role, keys, pricing and policies; #8 native telemetry mapping
and redaction. No mandatory CPAMP, custom read adapter or reporting store.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **A1:** A/B log in and see own keys/usage. A representative direct attempt to
  read B's history/detail as A is denied. Test the actual ordinary role selected.
- [ ] **A2:** Actual client works with nonstreaming/SSE Responses and tool/result
  continuation; exercise image/history/ancillary routes only when used. One upstream
  error and interrupted stream preserve behavior without partial-output replay.
- [ ] **A3:** A's keys aggregate to A and B stays separate. Compare sample response
  usage to retained native details/totals, including supplied cache/reasoning;
  missing measurements/pricing are explicit and subsets aren't double-counted.
  A completed native record survives restart.
- [ ] **A4:** One revoked-key and one model restriction denial cause no forbidden
  CPA request. Exercise a configured budget/rate limit, record native enforcement
  and propagation semantics, and avoid claiming strict concurrency guarantees.
- [ ] **A5:** The shared sample reaches Langfuse with trusted owner/session IDs and
  metadata-only payload, including content-bearing tool/image cases when used.
  Forged owner/session metadata cannot override mapping. Sink outage leaves
  inference usable and never replays provider work.
- [ ] **A6:** Healthy inference and native personal Usage work without CPAMP.
  Walk through history/native filters, record observed reporting lag and missing
  panels, and obtain baseline acceptance or a concrete gap decision in #1/#10.
- [ ] Record exact versions/config, client/route, sanitized results and limitations
  once for the run. Failures become focused integration fixes and retests.

## Non-goals

Exhaustive native endpoint/role/lifecycle testing, custom accounting infrastructure,
full crash-loss/replay or performance certification, or claiming deferred handoff
P1–P13 scenarios passed. Broaden tests for our custom behavior or a real failure.

## Operational notes

Use bounded synthetic traffic, keep secrets/content out of evidence and never
replay an ambiguous provider request to repair telemetry. #6 owns production
restore/cutover. Preserve `docs/live-acceptance.md` as historical old-path evidence.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md` A1–A6 and handoff mapping;
`docs/live-acceptance.md`; `scripts/live-acceptance.py`.

title: Configure native Langfuse: trusted attribution and metadata-only capture
body:
## Problem / outcome

Configure native LiteLLM Langfuse delivery with trusted personal attribution and
metadata-only capture. Reuse upstream transport; add code only if configuration
cannot provide an agreed owner/session or redaction requirement.

## Revision and current state

Approved October 29, 2026 revision. Original custom exporter contract is archived
in `docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`. `docs/exporter.md` and
existing exporter tests supply redaction/failure lessons; they are not a required
replacement implementation. Old null human-subject semantics differ from key owner.

## Scope

- Choose one supported native integration for the selected LiteLLM/SDK/destination.
- Configure stable deployment/owner-scoped user and session attribution from
  trusted server-side key state; untrusted sessions use a labeled request fallback.
- Disable content capture and keep bounded metadata, original timing, numeric
  usage and estimated cost. Inspect actual payload, not just configuration flags.
- Document native delivery behavior. A custom hook is conditional; a durable
  exporter/outbox requires a separate demonstrated requirement.

## Dependencies

#2 native stack/owner settings and Langfuse test endpoint. Joint verification
occurs in #7 A5 using the shared fixture, not a duplicate telemetry test suite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selected native callback, compatible versions and server-side credentials
  are configured and reproducible; duplicate exporters are not enabled.
- [ ] Trusted platform key owner maps to Langfuse user ID; caller `user` or trace/
  session metadata cannot impersonate an owner. Actor and key-owner meanings stay
  distinct; provider-account IDs are never substituted for people.
- [ ] #7 A5 confirms metadata-only actual payloads and sink-outage independence
  with the shared normal/stream/tool cases, including one forged-metadata case.
- [ ] Native delivery/loss/retry limitations are documented without a lossless or
  exactly-once claim. No telemetry failure causes provider replay.
- [ ] If custom mapping/redaction code is necessary, identify the exact native
  gap and add focused regression tests for that code; otherwise configuration
  alone completes this issue.

## Non-goals

Reimplementing Langfuse transport, a preplanned outbox, broad crash/ambiguous-ack
certification, raw content capture or Langfuse-based personal authorization.

## Operational notes

Use a separate test project, owner-scoped IDs and server-side secrets. Recording
native semantics does not establish durable delivery. #6 owns deployed retention
and credentials/recovery; update `DEVELOPMENT.md` with config and observed gaps.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md`; `docs/exporter.md`; handoff section 8.

title: Consolidated into #2: native personal keys and limit configuration
body:
## Problem / outcome

Use native personal virtual keys, model restrictions and limits. Consolidate
configuration into #2 and representative behavior checks into #7.

## Revision and current state

Approved consolidation into #2, October 29, 2026. Original group/application/custom-key
spec is archived in `docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`.
`docs/resources.md` and existing resource/policy code retain their old runtime
contract; no new native implementation or equivalence claim is needed here.

## Scope

#2 assigns stable personal owners and configures native keys/models/limits;
#7 checks attribution, revoked/model-denied requests and a configured limit.
Use documented native semantics. Stronger revocation or strict-budget guarantees
would need separate explicit scope rather than a duplicate upstream test project.

## Dependencies

#2 configuration; #7 A3/A4 integration acceptance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Personal key/limit configuration is in #2 and representative checks in #7.
- [ ] Original custom resource/key history remains preserved; old group-owned
  requests are not relabeled as personal based on their creator.
- Disposition: close as **not planned / consolidated into #2**, not successful
  completion of the old resource/policy runtime contract.

## Non-goals

Custom key/policy engine, exhaustive native lifecycle testing, group/Keycloak
integration or strict-budget/one-time-reveal equivalence by assumption.

## Operational notes

Record chosen native behavior and limitations. Old hashed-key import is not
assumed; #6 owns replacement-key issuance and historical-data treatment.

title: Deferred: personal reporting extensions for demonstrated native gaps
body:
## Problem / outcome

Add personal reporting only after native Usage demonstrates a concrete missing
capability the owner wants. Native totals/history/filters are configuration and
walkthrough work in #2/#7, not a new dashboard project.

## Revision and current state

Approved deferred disposition, October 29, 2026. Original CPAMP group projection
contract is archived in `docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`.
`docs/projection.md` and existing projection code remain current-runtime evidence.
Their source/ownership schema is not the proposed personal reporting source.

## Scope

Deferred gap inventory for possible reasoning/cache trends, latency/TTFT
percentiles, heatmaps, measured RPM/TPM, exports or session views. Native Usage
comes first. Before implementing, select one gap and split it into an independently
testable task with its required fields and UI/data/session boundary.

## Dependencies

#7 native walkthrough and gap findings; #1 explicit prioritization. No baseline
dependency on this issue, a new database, a custom read adapter or plugin embedding.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record the native capability, actual shortcoming and selected user outcome
  before opening implementation work. If native Usage suffices, defer this issue.
- [ ] For each selected gap, prefer supported scoped reads and a small extension;
  justify any new storage/capture and identify retained versus transient fields.
- [ ] Any custom reporting backend gets its own trusted session, owner-scoped
  queries/cache, isolation tests and clear unknown/freshness semantics.
- [ ] Any custom aggregation/capture gets focused tests for its metric definitions,
  normalization and deduplication/replay promises. These tests are conditional on
  code we add, not required to use the native dashboard.

## Non-goals

Baseline native UI implementation, full CPAMP parity, a broad UI fork, mandatory
plugins or SSO, a speculative personal ledger, or replacing group IDs with user IDs.

## Operational notes

If an extension becomes necessary, pin its interface, document session/edition
requirements and include custom state in #6 backup/retention. Advanced panels are
follow-up scope until explicitly prioritized. Do not claim callback-only data is
rebuildable after its source has discarded it.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md`; `docs/projection.md`; handoff sections 5–7.
